title: Reach every indexable page through a crawlable anchor href
statement: Each page the site wants indexed is reachable from at least one other indexable page by following anchor elements that carry a resolvable href attribute in the delivered document.
rationale: A crawler discovers pages by following hrefs, so a page linked only through a click handler, a form submission, or a script-built route has no discovery path and is found only if some other source happens to reveal its address.
implementation: Replace navigation built on click handlers with anchor elements carrying real hrefs, keeping any script behaviour as an enhancement on top. Where a route is only reachable through a form, add an equivalent linked entry point such as an index or archive page.

verification.method: Walk the anchor graph of the delivered documents from the home page and list route-inventory entries no walk reaches.

title: Allow crawlers to fetch the CSS and JavaScript the page needs to render
statement: No robots.txt rule or access control blocks the stylesheet and script resources a page requires to produce its primary content and layout.
rationale: An engine that renders the page fetches those resources under the same rules as the document, so blocking them produces a render missing its layout and, where content is script-generated, missing the content itself.
implementation: List the asset paths referenced by the delivered documents and test each against the robots.txt rules and any edge access rule. Narrow a broad disallow such as a whole build directory rather than adding a long list of allow exceptions beneath it.

verification.method: Evaluate the robots.txt directives against every render-critical asset URL referenced by a sampled page and record which ones are disallowed.

title: Bound the URL space that generated routes can produce
statement: Routes whose parameters are open-ended - calendars, arbitrary date ranges, internal search queries, unbounded coordinate or id spaces - are limited to a finite enumerable set or excluded from crawling.
rationale: An unbounded parameter lets a crawler generate new addresses indefinitely, and each fetch consumes capacity that would otherwise go to pages that hold real content.
implementation: For each dynamic segment, state the finite set of values the site intends to expose and reject the rest with 404. Where the space cannot be bounded, stop linking into it and disallow the path prefix instead of relying on the crawler to give up.

verification.method: Request a generated route with an out-of-range parameter value and record whether it returns content, an error status, or another set of links deeper into the same space.

sources.title: Large site owner's guide to managing your crawl budget

title: Expose primary navigation links in the document without a user gesture
statement: The links that make up the site's primary navigation are present in the delivered document, not added only after a hover, click, scroll, or consent interaction.
rationale: Automated fetchers do not perform gestures, so navigation that materializes only on interaction is absent from the document they see and the sections it leads to lose their main discovery path.
implementation: Render menu markup with its anchors in the initial document and use CSS or script only to control visibility. For a menu populated from an API, render the same link set server-side or provide a linked sitemap page that covers the destinations.

verification.method: Compare the set of anchors present before any interaction with the set present after opening every navigation control.

title: Serve the same primary content to crawlers and to readers
statement: The primary content, metadata, and directives in a response do not change based on the user agent, reverse DNS, or IP range of the requester; only genuinely device-dependent presentation may differ.
rationale: Detecting a crawler and serving it different material is cloaking under published platform policy, and it also removes the site's ability to see what the engine actually receives.
implementation: Search the request-handling path, edge rules, and CDN configuration for user-agent branching that affects content or directives, and remove the branch. Where a bot rule exists for rate limiting, confirm it changes throughput only and never the response body.

verification.method: Request the same URL with a browser user agent and with a documented crawler user agent, then diff the primary content, metadata, and status of the two responses.

sources.title: Spam policies for Google web search

title: Declare which filter and sort combinations are crawlable
statement: The site states explicitly which faceted combinations are meant to be crawled and indexed, and combinations outside that set are neither linked with crawlable hrefs nor listed in a sitemap.
rationale: Facets combine multiplicatively, so a handful of independent filters produces more addresses than the site has content, and without a declared allowlist the crawler has no way to tell the valuable combinations from the rest.
implementation: Write the intended combinations down as data - which facets, how many at once, which values - and drive both link generation and sitemap inclusion from it. Render the excluded combinations behind controls that do not produce crawlable hrefs rather than blocking them after the fact.

verification.method: Enumerate the facet URLs reachable by following hrefs from a listing page and compare that set against the declared allowlist.

title: Expose a finite pagination path to the last page of every sequence
statement: Every paginated sequence can be traversed to its final page by following hrefs, and requesting a page number beyond the end returns a not-found status rather than an empty successful page.
rationale: A sequence with no reachable end, or one that answers 200 for any page number, presents an endless supply of near-empty addresses and hides the items on the real later pages behind an unbounded walk.
implementation: Compute the total page count when rendering the control and stop emitting a next link at the end. Validate the requested page number against that total in the route handler and return 404 when it exceeds the total.

verification.method: Follow next links from the first page of a sequence until they stop, then request one page beyond the final number and record the status returned.
